The Rise of the Yeke Kingdom

\n\nWord has come to us about a Yeke trader by the name of Msiri from Tabora. He was a trader, like his father Kalasa, involved in the copper, ivory and slave trade controlled by the Sultan of Zanzibar and his Arab and Swahili agents. The main trade route went to Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika and then to Lake Mweru and Katanga. Msiri realized access to guns was the key to power, and in Katanga, he had copper and ivory resources to trade for them. He formed a militia and started to conquer his neighbors, eventually declaring the Yeke Kingdom.
The End of the American Civil War

With the final surrender of Confederate forces to the Union armies, President Andrew Johnson has signed a Proclamation - Declaring that Peace, Order, Tranquility, and Civil Authority Now Exists in and Throughout the Whole of the United States of America. It cited the end of the insurrection in Texas, and declared - 

"... that the insurrection which heretofore existed in the State of Texas is at an end and is to be henceforth so regarded in that State as in the other States before named in which the said insurrection was proclaimed to be at an end by the aforesaid proclamation. 
And I do further proclaim that the said insurrection is at an end and that peace, order, tranquility, and civil authority now exist in and throughout the whole of the United States of America." The Union has prevailed.

The Society of Heaven and Earth

The Tiandihui, also known as the Heaven and Earth Association was known to be founded by Chinese patriots in the 17th century for the purpose of overthrowing the Qing Dynasty and restoring the Ming Dynasty. Originating in the Changchow area of Fukien, by the beginning of the 19th century the Tiandihui had spread to nearly all of southern China. 

Tiandihui secret societies were typically involved in both revolutionary activity and organized crime, such as piracy and opium smuggling. Many members of the Tiandihui were typically poor peasants, handicraftsmen, nomads and bandits.
We shall keep an eye out for secret societies.

\n\nFollowing in the footsteps of Hong Xiuquan's uprising, the local Tiandihui and their tribes responded with enthusiasm and quickly followed suit with their own uprisings in the Canton, Kwangsi and Fukien provinces. Taking advantage of the disarray of Qing forces, the rebels took the opportunity to launch a general attack, occupying the city of Changchow, renaming it Xiujing. The rebels would soon attempt to seize the provincial capital of Guangzhou (Canton).
